MUNICIPAL REVIEWER — Cycle 1, 07 Aug 2026. Decision: VERIFY (not approved).

Finding — IRC:78 Cl. 703.3.1 not satisfied. The sole scour computation (Appendix D.4, pier P2) adopts the 1-in-50-year flood, peak discharge 2,180 m3/s. The design flood for this crossing, per the standard and per the design report itself, is the 1-in-100-year flood, 2,450 m3/s. Cl. 703.3.1 states that a computation for a lesser flood does not dimension the works for the design flood. The founding level (96.40 m) and the riprap apron (3.0 m, 1.2 m thick) are therefore dimensioned from an under-sized flood and cannot be accepted as compliant.

Why this is material here: BH-3 records 4.2 m of loose to very loose fine sand (SPT 4-7) with groundwater 1.1 m below bed; BH-4 records 3.6 m of similar sand. The geotechnical report recommends a scour computation for the design flood in both the body and the executive summary and supplies none. The design report calls P2 the deepest foundation "on the crossing" while citing BH-3/BH-4 as loose sand to 12.4 m — the basis of that 12.4 m depth is not reconciled with the borehole log and must be shown.

Required before a decision. Contractor to submit a re-run Appendix D.4 for the 1-in-100-year flood (2,450 m3/s), signed by the design engineer, stating the flood adopted, the resulting scour depth, founding level and protection dimensions, and confirming the founded depth and apron remain adequate for it; and to reconcile the loose-sand depth at P2/P3 with the founding level adopted. Checker to record a finding on resubmission.

Note on pressure: the end-September opening and the booked ceremony are not compliance grounds. The crossing being replaced was destroyed in flood with eleven lives lost; releasing a crossing whose scour protection is dimensioned to half the design flood risk would not be defensible at the quarterly audit. The hold is on approval only — the package can return and be approved this season if the re-run computation clears.
